Fixed 1 Aug — the lightbox <iframe> is injected via JS innerHTML, so it never picked up Astro's scoped-style attribute; the CSS meant to size it to the modal (width/height:100%) silently never matched, so it fell back to the browser's ~300x150 default. Fixed by setting size inline on the iframe string (same pattern schools.astro already used). Same root cause found and fixed on /why too (not separately reported).
How Change Happens ripple/orbit shows static (no pin/scroll choreography) on a real iPhone 15 Pro + Chrome; looks perfect on desktop Chrome and Chrome's device toolbar mobile emulation.

Not a bug — diagnosed 1 Aug. Root cause: the device has iOS's Reduce Motion accessibility setting on; Chrome for iOS runs on WebKit and honors it, and orbit.js/global.css already intentionally fall back to a static stacked layout under prefers-reduced-motion (by design, per ACCESSIBILITY.md). Chrome's device toolbar/window resizing does not flip that media feature, which is why desktop testing looked fine — reproduced instead via DevTools Rendering tab "Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion: reduce", which produced the identical static result. No code fix; left behavior as-is. Added comments at the reduced-motion branches in orbit.js and global.css so the team doesn't re-diagnose this from scratch next time.
